teams.heading: Koli Sewabu says Fiji are following Mark Nawaqanitawase's possible switch with interest
teams.body: Fiji Rugby Union chief executive Koli Sewabu says the union is watching closely after Mark Nawaqanitawase's agent revealed the winger is weighing a switch of allegiance. Nawaqanitawase, eligible for Fiji, Italy and Australia after a three-year stand-down, won 11 Wallabies caps. "We are aware of the potential switch Mark could make at the next World Cup and follow this with interest," Sewabu said. Wallabies head coach Les Kiss says he will wait until the end of the year to see where the player sits.

lead.why: It is the only new item in the pack that directly concerns a Fiji player and the union's own response, and it is the story a fan would most likely be discussing.

teams.heading: Courtney Lawes and Ellis Genge question England's overseas eligibility rule on podcast
teams.body: England loosehead Ellis Genge has said on The Good, The Bad and The Rugby podcast: "I don't think it's fair to say you ain't allowed to do it." Genge, 83 caps, backed a 60-cap threshold before a player can move abroad, while forward Courtney Lawes, 105 caps and freshly back from two seasons at Brive, pointed to Wales' 25-cap model as a possible compromise. The current rule, barring overseas-based players save in exceptional circumstances since 2012, is built to protect the Premiership.

teams.heading: Thibaud Flament facing weeks out with shoulder injury, weakening France's second row
teams.body: Toulouse lock Thibaud Flament is facing several weeks on the sidelines with a shoulder injury, according to L'Équipe, a fresh blow for France coach Fabien Galthié as he readies his pack for the Springboks in Paris. Flament, 29, played the full 80 minutes of Toulouse's 45-34 Top 14 win over Bayonne on Sunday, and had been tipped to partner France's second row against Fiji, the Springboks and Argentina. Emmanuel Meafou is already expected to be without him too, as he recovers from a knee injury.

lead.why: It is the only men's France story in the pack that is hard news about the squad, a lock injury that weakens the second row before the Springboks test.

teams.heading: Leo Cullen's Leinster enter Champions Cup with weaker squad after summer exits
teams.body: Leinster arguably enter the Champions Cup this weekend with a weaker squad than usual, BBC Sport NI says, after James Lowe, Rieko Ioane, Rabah Slimani and Ciaran Frawley all left over the summer. Only Frawley has been replaced in kind, by Joey Carbery, but the 30-year-old is yet to feature in his second stint because of injury. Munster, dropped into the Challenge Cup after a home defeat to Castres last season, are also starting out.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item on the shortlist, and it covers how all four Irish provinces enter the Champions Cup this weekend.

teams.heading: Italy average 17.3 points a game scored over their last 11 matches
teams.body: Over their last 11 matches, Italy have scored 190 points in total, an average of 17.3 a game. The bill has been heavier at the other end: across the same 11 games they have conceded 318, or 28.9 a game. Their biggest win in that stretch was a 34-19 home victory over Chile in November 2025, in an International Friendlies fixture.

teams.heading: Scotland have won three and lost two of their last five games
teams.body: In their last five games, Scotland have won three and lost two, with results alternating W L W L W from most recent to oldest. The latest of those was a 33-17 win over Fiji, played away in July's Nations Championship group stage. Three wins and two defeats from five makes for a steady rather than streaking record.

teams.heading: Kieran Hardy faces knee surgery and months out, a blow to Wales
teams.body: Kieran Hardy, Ospreys and Wales scrum-half, needs knee surgery and faces months rather than weeks out, Ospreys transition coach Richard Kelly confirmed. Hardy, 30, was helped off in the first half of the 38-31 win at Dragons and had been expected to feature in Wales' November Tests. He was understudy to Gloucester scrum-half Tomos Williams in the 2026 Six Nations, and BBC Sport judges him a serious doubt for next year's championship too, which could intensify calls for former Wales scrum-half Gareth Davies to reverse his retirement.

lead.why: A new Wales and Ospreys scrum-half injury with knee surgery and a likely Six Nations knock-on, which is hard news that matters more to Wales than the other items.

teams.heading: Verdicts expected in Paris trial over killing of Argentina player Aramburú
teams.body: Verdicts are expected in the trial in Paris over the killing of Argentina rugby player Aramburú. Today's coverage gives no date for the verdicts, and the outcome is not yet reported. The Pumas' next match is Ireland in Round 4 of the Nations Championship, with Italy and France also on the November list. Shaun Edwards and Mario Ledesma, the new coaching additions, start work with the Pumas at the end of October.

teams.heading: Declan Meredith starts at fly-half as Ben Donaldson misses second Bledisloe
teams.body: Head coach Les Kiss has given Brumbies playmaker Declan Meredith his fourth start at fly-half for Saturday's second Bledisloe Test in Sydney, after Ben Donaldson failed to come through training on Thursday with a minor upper-leg injury. Carter Gordon is also out with a leg injury, so Western Force recruit Harry McLaughlin-Phillips is set for a Test debut off the bench. Kiss said the Wallabies got "a clear picture" from the 50-19 loss at Eden Park.

lead.why: Donaldson's failed training check makes Meredith's start a fresh, Australia-side selection story, not a repeat of the Wednesday Suaalii item.

teams.heading: Japan go to Wales after 15-42 defeat by France in Round three
teams.body: Japan's next match is Wales in Round four, coming off a 15-42 defeat to France in Round three. Their most recent meeting with Wales ended 24-23 in Wales' favour, a November 2025 game played away for Japan. Japan's log record so far is one win, no draws and two defeats, with 62 points scored and 88 conceded, a points difference of -26.

teams.heading: Fabian Holland replaces Josh Lord in All Blacks second row for Sydney
teams.body: Fabian Holland returns to the All Blacks second row for Saturday's second Bledisloe Test in Sydney, replacing Josh Lord after being left out at Eden Park. Dave Rennie, the All Blacks head coach, has made eight changes to his matchday 23, and the 2025 World Rugby Breakthrough Player of the Year, who starred against the Springboks, partners Scott Barrett in the engine room. Leroy Carter's high ankle sprain also forces Josh Moorby onto the left wing.

lead.why: Holland's recall is the clearest hard selection news in the pack, and it is a New Zealand story about the men's XV.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie says Springboks are not dominant under the high ball
teams.body: Dave Rennie, the All Blacks head coach, told reporters that no side in the world dominates the ball kicked to it, South Africa included, and that his side's tactic of tracking back to block for aerial contests is no secret. He said roughly one in four kicks is caught cleanly by the receiving team. The claim pushes back on a perception that New Zealand are especially vulnerable under the high ball, a weakness Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus' men have exploited in the air.

lead.why: It is the freshest item that is squarely about the Springboks' own aerial game, while the other new items are club, Fiji or referee-development stories.
